text: Family Circle is a public artwork by American artist Herbert House, situated at the intersection of 18th and Harvard Streets NW in the Adams Morgan neighborhood of Washington, D.C., United States. The sculpture was dedicated in 1991 and was surveyed as part of the Smithsonian's Save Outdoor Sculpture! initiative in 1994. It features four nude figures—male, female, and two children—dancing in a circle, crafted from cut and welded car bumpers. The figures are made of highly polished steel and lack facial features, feet, and hands. They are positioned on a red circular tilted platform. Herbert House grew up in Washington, D.C., graduated from Illinois State University, and is credited with creating over 500 works. He currently resides in Chicago, Illinois, and his artwork is held in the collections of Illinois State University and various private collections. The sculpture was described in 1994 as "well maintained." In 2017, it was vandalized when two of the figures were torn off the platform. In 2018, the city hired Herbert House to repair the sculpture, after which it was restored and returned to public display.
